experiments.name: address-bypass pointer chase
experiments.notes: The stored experiment is the direct address chase (4 cycles). The second case puts add.d in the address path and measures 5, the general load latency. A third check, fld.d -> fadd.d -> movfr2gr.d -> address, gives the same 4 cycles for the data path, so the extra cycle belongs to the address path, not to the data path.

latencies.notes: 3 cycles of helper latency are subtracted. Unroll 10000, iters 1000. Raw measurement was 3.99; the residual is a systematic calibration offset, so the recorded value is the nominal integer with the observed spread.

cases.name: load result feeds the next address directly
load result passes through add.d before the next address

experiment.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r13, $sp, -1016; st.d $r13, $r13, 0; addi.d $r4, $r13, 0; li.d $r5, 0' --asm 'fld.d $f0, $r4, 0; movfr2gr.d $r4, $f0; add.d $r4, $r4, $r5'

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024' --asm 'fld.d $f0, $r20, 0; fld.d $f1, $r20, 8; fld.d $f2, $r20, 16; fld.d $f3, $r20, 24; fld.d $f4, $r20, 32; fld.d $f5, $r20, 40; fld.d $f6, $r20, 48; fld.d $f7, $r20, 56'

notes: L1D-hit floating-point load. Two address paths: 4 cycles when the loaded value becomes the next address directly (address bypass, the pointer chase), 5 cycles when an ALU operation sits between the load result and the address, the same 4/5 split as ld.d. The data path to an FP consumer is also 4 cycles (measured with fadd.d in the loop). Measured with --method slope on LA464, core 0.
